title: Acadia National Park Trip Planner Printable, Acadia Itinerary, Bar Harbor Maine Travel Guide, Best Day Hikes, Cadillac Mountain PDF
description:
Planning a first trip to Acadia National Park in Maine? This 30-page printable guide puts the whole trip on paper: when to go, what to book and when, how to get around without fighting for parking, and how to spend 1, 2 or 3 days.

WHAT'S INSIDE
- The park at a glance: Mount Desert Island, the quiet side, the Schoodic Peninsula and Isle au Haut, with rough drive times from Bangor, Portland, Boston and Saint John NB in miles and km
- When to go, season by season: summer crowds, fall color, mud season and what closes in winter
- Passes and fees: 2026 entrance fees, annual passes, the non-resident fee, and a note for visitors from Canada
- Reservations: how the Cadillac Summit Road sunrise and daytime slots and the campground bookings open, plus a booking tracker you fill in
- Getting around: the free Island Explorer bus, parking that fills early, bikes and e-bike rules on the carriage roads
- Where to stay: the three park campgrounds, Bar Harbor, the quiet side and towns off the island, with a comparison you fill in
- Sample 1, 2 and 3-day plans, a rainy-day plan and a low-tide plan for the Bar Island land bridge
- Sunrise on Cadillac Mountain: what to know and what to wear on a cold summit
- 12 day hikes, easy to very hard, from the Ocean Path, Jordan Pond and the Bubbles to the iron-rung Beehive and Precipice, with NPS distances in mi and km
- Carriage roads, safety on granite (wet rock, fog, cliffs, tides), wildlife, packing list, kids and dogs, day planner, hike log, budget and trip checklist

WHAT YOU GET
- US Letter and A4 versions
- Mobile edition, sized for reading on your phone
- Color and printer-friendly (low ink) versions
- Instant download. This is a digital file; nothing is shipped.
- Bonus: our free one-page Ultimate Hiking Checklist

GOOD TO KNOW
Checked against nps.gov in November 2026. Acadia changes its reservation dates, fees, road openings and trail closures from year to year, so check the official park website for your dates before you book. The Beehive and Precipice use iron rungs on cliffs and are not for anyone afraid of heights. No maps or GPS files. Not affiliated with the National Park Service. For personal use.

Made by HikeSupply Co., a small shop for weekend hikers. More printable hiking guides in our Etsy shop.
